title: Question Tags
content:
Definition

English: Question tags are short questions added to the end of a statement to confirm or seek agreement, often using an auxiliary verb and pronoun.
Hindi: Question tags chhote prashn hote hain jo vakya ke ant mein jode jate hain taaki pushti ya sahmati maangi jaye, aksar sahayak kriya aur sarvanam ke saath.

They turn a statement into a question or emphasize agreement.
Ye ek vakya ko prashn mein badalte hain ya sahmati par zor dete hain.

Example: She is coming, isn't she?
Hindi: Woh aa rahi hai, hai na?

title: Structure of Question Tags
content:
Rules

English: A question tag consists of an auxiliary verb (or main verb 'be') and a pronoun matching the subject. If the statement is positive, the tag is negative, and vice versa.
Hindi: Question tag mein sahayak kriya (ya mukhya kriya 'be') aur karta se milta-julta sarvanam hota hai. Agar vakya sakaratmak hai, to tag nakaaratmak hota hai, aur iske vipreet.

Structure

Auxiliary Verb (opposite polarity) + Subject Pronoun

Example: You are tired, aren't you?
Hindi: Tum thak gaye ho, hai na?

title: Positive Statement with Negative Tag
content:
Use

English: Used when the main statement is positive, expecting confirmation or agreement.
Hindi: Jab mukhya vakya sakaratmak ho, to pushti ya sahmati ke liye prayog hota hai.

Structure

Positive Statement + Negative Auxiliary + Subject Pronoun

Example: He plays football, doesn't he?
Hindi: Woh football khelta hai, hai na?

title: Negative Statement with Positive Tag
content:
Use

English: Used when the main statement is negative, seeking confirmation or clarification.
Hindi: Jab mukhya vakya nakaaratmak ho, to pushti ya spashtikaran ke liye prayog hota hai.

Structure

Negative Statement + Positive Auxiliary + Subject Pronoun

Example: She didn't go, did she?
Hindi: Woh nahi gayi, gayin na?

title: Question Tags with Different Tenses
content:
Explanation

Hindi: Question tag mein sahayak kriya mukhya vakya ke tense aur kriya se milti hai.

Examples by Tense

  • Present Simple: You know him, don't you?
    Hindi: Tum use jaante ho, hai na?
  • Past Simple: They left early, didn't they?
    Hindi: Ve jaldi chale gaye, hai na?
  • Present Perfect: She has finished, hasn't she?
    Hindi: Usne kaam pura kar liya, hai na?
  • Future Simple: He will come, won't he?
    Hindi: Woh aayega, hai na?
Example (Present Continuous): They are studying, aren't they?
Hindi: Ve padh rahe hain, hai na?

title: Special Cases in Question Tags
content:
Explanation

English: Some statements require specific tags: 1) 'I am' uses 'aren't I?', 2) Imperatives use 'will you?', 3) 'Let's' uses 'shall we?', 4) No auxiliary in simple present/past uses 'do/does/did'.
Hindi: Kuch vakyas mein vishesh tags lagte hain: 1) 'I am' ke liye 'aren't I?', 2) Aadesh ke liye 'will you?', 3) 'Let's' ke liye 'shall we?', 4) Simple present/past mein bina sahayak kriya ke 'do/does/did' ka prayog.

Examples:
  • I am late, aren't I?
    Hindi: Main der se hoon, hai na?
  • Open the door, will you?
    Hindi: Darwaza kholo, karoge?
  • Let's go, shall we?
    Hindi: Chalo, chalein?

title: Uses of Question Tags
content:
Use

English: Question tags are used to: 1) Seek confirmation, 2) Express doubt or surprise, 3) Engage in conversation, 4) Soften statements.
Hindi: Question tags ka prayog hota hai: 1) Pushti mangne ke liye, 2) Sanshay ya ashcharya vyakt karne ke liye, 3) Baat-cheet mein shamil karne ke liye, 4) Vakya ko naram banane ke liye.

Example: You can drive, can't you? (Seeking confirmation)
Hindi: Tum car chala sakte ho, hai na? (Pushti ke liye)
